article_title: Somali piracy surges as the impact of the US-Iran war ripples outwards

tasks.prompt: What is the article's central argument?
options: Regional conflict and reduced maritime deterrence have created new opportunities for Somali piracy to rise
Somali piracy has ended because all commercial shipping now avoids the Indian Ocean
The Houthi movement directly commands every pirate network operating near Somalia
Foreign fishing has become Somalia's largest source of government revenue
tasks.correct_answer: Regional conflict and reduced maritime deterrence have created new opportunities for Somali piracy to rise
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הטענה המרכזית היא שהמלחמה, החסימות והפחתת ההרתעה הימית יוצרים הזדמנות מחודשת לרשתות פיראטיות סומליות.

tasks.prompt: How many ships had been attacked since the start of the year when the article was published?
options: At least six
At least 13
More than 50
More than 200
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מדווחת כי מספר הספינות שהותקפו מתחילת השנה עלה ל־13 לפחות.

tasks.prompt: Which description of the MV Lutuf is accurate?
options: It is an Eritrean oil-products tanker seized near Yemen
It is a Spanish naval vessel patrolling the Red Sea
It is a Cameroon-flagged ship hijacked off Puntland on 17 August
It is an Iranian vessel released without a ransom demand
tasks.correct_answer: It is a Cameroon-flagged ship hijacked off Puntland on 17 August
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ה־MV Lutuf היא ספינה בדגל קמרון שנחטפה מול חופי פונטלנד ב־17 באוגוסט.

tasks.prompt: Why can conflict around Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb benefit pirates operating farther south?
options: It makes ransom payments illegal in every country
It prevents pirates from approaching the Somali coast
It causes foreign trawlers to stop fishing permanently
It can divert naval attention while pushing more commercial ships into waters accessible to pirates
tasks.correct_answer: It can divert naval attention while pushing more commercial ships into waters accessible to pirates
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המשברים בצפון עשויים להסיט כוחות ימיים ובמקביל להביא יותר ספינות מסחריות לנתיבים הקרובים לסומליה.

tasks.prompt: What does “scourge” mean when the article says an international response drove it down?
options: A profitable new shipping route
A serious and persistent problem causing harm
A formal agreement between two governments
A device used to track hijacked vessels
tasks.correct_answer: A serious and persistent problem causing harm
tasks.explanation_hebrew: scourge מתאר תופעה מזיקה וקשה המתמשכת לאורך זמן — כאן, הפיראטיות.

tasks.prompt: What does the phrase “ripples outwards” in the headline suggest?
options: The war's effects are limited to the Strait of Hormuz
Pirates are creating physical waves to stop ships
The conflict's consequences spread beyond its immediate centre to other regions
Shipping companies have completely solved the regional crisis
tasks.correct_answer: The conflict's consequences spread beyond its immediate centre to other regions
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הביטוי מתאר כיצד השלכות המלחמה מתפשטות מעבר לזירתה הישירה ומשפיעות גם על נתיבי שיט ליד סומליה.

tasks.prompt: Explain the combination of international and local conditions that is enabling the piracy surge.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לשלב גורמים אזוריים ובין־לאומיים עם גורמים כלכליים וביטחוניים מקומיים בסומליה.
expected_points: The US-Iran war is straining regional waterways
Conflict at Hormuz and the Houthi blockade at Bab el-Mandeb absorb attention
Naval patrols may be reduced or redirected
Some commercial ships divert closer to the Somali coast
High oil prices make tankers more valuable targets
Pirate networks were suppressed but remained intact
Poor economic and security conditions continue to feed recruitment
Anger over foreign trawlers damaging Puntland's fishing industry fuels local support
Successful attacks can encourage copycat incidents

tasks.prompt: Distinguish confirmed facts from allegations or unverified claims about the Lutuf and the drone strikes.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין בבירור מה ידוע, מה נטען בידי מקורות מקומיים ומה ה־BBC לא הצליח לאמת עצמאית.
expected_points: The Lutuf was hijacked off Puntland on 17 August
Thirteen alleged members of a pirate supply network were killed in two drone strikes
No actor publicly claimed responsibility for the strikes
Local officials blamed Turkey
Sources alleged the ship carried weapons for a Turkish training facility
A Somali official alleged that Turkey carried out the second strike
Turkey said it was providing necessary support under its security agreement
Turkey did not directly address the accusations about the deadly strikes
The BBC could not independently verify the claims about warships or Turkish responsibility

tasks.prompt: Summarise the scale, causes and risks of the current rise in Somali piracy.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול נתונים על ההתקפות, לפחות שלושה גורמים לעלייה, השוואה לעבר והסיכון להמשך.
expected_points: At least 13 ships had been attacked since the start of the year
Two cargo vessels were seized within four days
Six vessels were being held for multimillion-dollar ransom demands
Regional war and blockades may reduce naval attention
Diversions bring more commercial targets closer to Somalia
High oil prices increase the potential value of tanker hijackings
Local poverty, insecurity and anger over foreign fishing sustain pirate networks
The level remains far below the more than 200 attacks in 2011
Political tension between Puntland and Mogadishu complicates a coordinated response
Without stronger deterrence or an end to the wider war, the threat may continue

tasks.prompt: Propose a balanced regional response to the piracy surge. Use evidence from the article and address both immediate security and underlying causes.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציע תגובה מאוזנת באנגלית הכוללת הרתעה מיידית, תיאום מדיני וטיפול בגורמי העומק, תוך הסתמכות על הכתבה.
expected_points: Restore coordinated international naval patrols in high-risk waters
Support private security and practical protection on commercial vessels
Improve information-sharing among Somalia, Puntland and international forces
Investigate attacks and drone strikes transparently to avoid escalation
Protect lawful fishing and address damaging foreign overfishing
Create economic opportunities for coastal communities
Strengthen Somali maritime security institutions
Avoid treating unverified allegations as established facts
Plan for the displacement of shipping caused by Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb
Combine deterrence with long-term action on poverty and insecurity
